title: Capacity triage: hybrid queue with adaptive fidelity ladders
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Recent multi-region incident (2026-02-28) exposed that a single aggressive spike caused tail-latency violations and then a cascade of expensive model fallbacks. We need a service-level triage admission layer (Capacity Triage) that enforces SLOs by routing requests into hybrid lanes and applying graduated fidelity reductions before failing. Goal: keep critical SLOs (p95 latency < configured SLO, error rate < configured threshold) for high-tier tenants while minimizing overall user-facing failures and preserving cost predictability.

Proposal: Implement a stateless triage service + runtime hooks that calculates a per-request triage decision and assigns one of four lanes: instant (low-latency path, no batching), balanced (medium latency with small batching), batched (high throughput via batching + KV-prefix caching), degraded (fidelity-limited response / summary / small-model fallback). Admission decisions combine tenant SLA weight, request deadline, estimated token cost, historical cache-hit probability, and region health score. Integrate with existing circuit-breaker signals to immediately short-circuit to cached/quantized variants when model error rate or GPU queue depth exceeds thresholds.

Why different from prior approaches: Rather than purely token-bucket or lane-count thresholds, this design uses a blended triage score and enforces soft budgets per-tenant and per-region with graceful degradation options that can be targeted to request types (e.g., streaming chat vs. single-shot generation). The goal is to reduce noisy neighbor effects while providing deterministic rollback options during failover and region outages.
decision_log: 2026-03-11 — Proposal approved by Eng Leads (Priya Kapoor): adopt blended triage score combining SLA weight + deadline slack + est_token_cost. Keep initial lane set to 4. Action: prototype triage module in runtime gateway.
2026-03-12 — Security (Liam O'Neill): flagged KMS usage for fallback artifacts; we must ensure cache keys don't leak PII. Action: add data-class labels to triage decisions for audit logs.
2026-03-13 — Perf (Nora Jensen): synthetic load tests show balanced lane increases p95 by 15ms but reduces token cost by 12%. Agree to tune batching windows per model family.
2026-03-14 — PM review (Samira Rahman): require a clear rollback plan and observability dashboard before beta rollout; include tenant-level SLO exposures.

Design trade-offs considered: conservative default thresholds to avoid user-visible regressions vs. aggressive cost-saving defaults; we chose conservative defaults with a remote-flag for aggressive mode.
comments: 2026-03-11 Marcus V: Initial skeleton PR created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/triage-service/pull/42). Wireframes for console config in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Capacity+Triage+Config

2026-03-12 Ava C: Ran incident replay with the prototype triage. Observed 27% fewer fallbacks to large-model endpoints when triage enabled in simulation mode. Saved tokens metric attached to test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/incident-replay/triage-sim

2026-03-13 Nora J: Added test for circuit-breaker handoff to cached-smaller models. Found race where cache warmup correlated with wrong lane assignment; fixed by adding cache-hit probability smoothing over 30s.
2026-03-14 Samira R: Reviewed UX for tenant controls (canary percentage, SLA weight override). PM requests additional label: customer_impact at rollout stage.
acceptance_criteria: Triaged requests annotated in trace with lane and triage_score for 99% of traffic in canary region
p95 latency for P0 tenants remains within configured SLO during 2x synthetic spike test
Fallbacks to smaller/quantized models triggered automatically when regional queue depth > threshold and error rate > threshold
Dashboard: per-tenant exposure, lane distribution, triage_score histogram, cache-hit smoothing metric
Runbook entry created that documents rollback steps, circuit-breaker thresholds, and customer communication templates
